title: Noorani
conceptQuote: "Where Mughal grandeur meets the raw spirit of a warrior queen."
conceptBody: Noorani is a womenswear collection rooted in the complex emotional landscape of Mughal-era India — power, devotion, tragedy, and defiance. The name, meaning luminous in Urdu, speaks to the radiant femininity that persists even in darkness.
conceptRight: Drawing inspiration from the cinematic world of Bajirao Mastani, each look channels a distinct emotional archetype — Tegh (the sword), Ehsaas (the feeling), Ulfat (affection), Deewani (the devoted), Ehad (the vow), Noorjahan (the queen of light), Qaid (captivity), and Fanaa (dissolution).

The silhouettes merge historical Indian craft traditions — zardosi embroidery, banarasi weaves, kantha work — with contemporary structural tailoring. Colours move from ivory and dust-gold through rich reds and purples to forest greens and near-black, tracing an emotional arc from vulnerability to sovereignty.

looks.name: Tegh
looks.description: Tegh — the sword. A warrior's silhouette rendered in ivory and burnished gold. A structured bralette of hand-embroidered zardosi work sits above a fluid ivory drape skirt, the hard meets the soft, armour meets grace. Inspired by the fearless Mastani mid-duel.

looks.name: Ehsaas
looks.description: Ehsaas — feeling. A soft column of pale blush chiffon falls from a structured gold-embroidered corset. A voluminous ivory shawl — half-draped, half-abandoned — speaks of intimacy interrupted. The quietest look in the collection, and perhaps its most vulnerable.

looks.name: Ulfat
looks.description: Ulfat — affection. A deep crimson anarkali, densely embroidered with floral zardosi, worn over a wine-red lehenga. A three-dimensional rose crowns the shoulder. Gold-ankled boots bring the look into a contemporary register, refusing pure nostalgia.

looks.name: Deewani
looks.description: Deewani — the devoted. A look of all-consuming gold. A sheer tissue-silk gown is layered with tasselled fringe and paisley embroidery; a dramatic gilded halo headpiece echoes the ecstatic devotion of a kotha dancer. Intoxicating and dangerous in equal measure.

looks.name: Ehad
looks.description: Ehad — the vow. Sage-green meets burnt rose. A halter-neck kurta of kantha-embroidered dupion silk is worn over a layered lehenga of contrasting dusty rose brocade. The hooded sage dupatta recalls a bridal veil and a warrior's shield simultaneously.

looks.name: Noorjahan
looks.description: Noorjahan — the queen of light. Deep plum velvet over an embellished forest-green micro skirt, a long draped train of wine banarasi silk trailing behind. Ruby and pearl necklaces layer at the throat. Regal, complex, untouchable.

looks.name: Qaid
looks.description: Qaid — captivity. A cropped velvet jacket in dark wine over a midriff-baring bralette, paired with draped harem trousers in deep tobacco-brown printed silk. Heavy ankle cuffs and green-stone jewels complete a look that makes captivity look like a choice.

looks.name: Fanaa
looks.description: Fanaa — dissolution. The collection ends in dark forest green and near-black. A raw-hemmed asymmetric kurta dress in olive tissue-silk, layered with a dark banarasi border, worn with embroidered black equestrian boots. The fire has burnt everything away. Only the dress remains.

title: Adirath
conceptBody: Adirath is a menswear collection that explores the duality of strength and vulnerability through the lens of ancient Indian warrior culture. The name means great charioteer in Sanskrit — a nod to those who carry others into battle.
conceptRight: The collection draws from Mahabharata-era silhouettes, reinterpreting the dhoti-kurta and angavastram through a contemporary tailoring lens. Heavy linens meet hand-block printed cottons, structured shoulders echo pauldrons, and raw edges speak of battles yet to be fought.
The palette centres on raw sand, undyed khadi, deep indigo, aged iron, and burnished bronze — materials that tell the story of men who shaped history with their hands.

title: The Entangled Souls
conceptQuote: "Two bodies, one spirit — where love dissolves the self."
conceptBody: The Entangled Souls is a womenswear collection exploring the philosophy of advaita — non-duality — through fashion. Each garment is designed to feel incomplete alone, only revealing its full form when worn in relationship to another piece.
conceptRight: Inspired by the mystical poetry of Mirabai and Rumi, the collection uses fabric manipulation — interlocking cuts, shared seams, dual-sided garments — to create pieces that physically enact the concept of interconnection.
The palette centres on deep indigo, midnight purple, and silver-white — the colours of night sky and moonlight, of the space between two people who have become one.
